data.name: Brave Hand
data.detailed_description:
Developer's Note

This is the desktop version of my push-your-luck card game Brave Hand. Please expect Brave Hand to be a small, replayable, solitaire-like card game where your goal is to beat your previous score, and unlock a light story along the way. I made it because I loved the simple yet replayable games that came with my first computer, and wanted something like them, but with just a little more strategy. If the main "Brave" mode is too hard or too random for your taste, be sure to try out the other modes! Each mode is designed to cater to a specific type of playstyle. Please contact me through Twitter, our forums, or my website if you run into any trouble or just want to follow along with development. I really hope you enjoy the game. -Scott Brodie


Acerca do jogo

Scott Brodie Estas numa ilha misteriosa e desenterras um jogo velho e esquecido de cartas. À medida que jogas, começas a desvendar partes do segredo de sua origem, estratégia e poderes escondidos. Será suficientemente corajoso para prosseguires e descobrires todos os seus segredos?

Brave Hand é um jogo de cartas original, em que jogas individualmente, que irá testar a tua sorte. Incrivelmente simples porém profundamente estratégico. Ao jogar, irás desvendar a história do Viajante e do Guardião, através de 16 belíssimos temas pintados a mão. Um design elegante que combina a simplicidade dos jogos clássicos de cartas como War, a audácia de um jogo de Poker e a estratégia dos jogos de colecção de cartas.

Brave Hand inspirou-se no desejo de criar um jogo individual de cartas mais estratégicos. O jogo usa o estilo de jogo de Paciência e melhora-o com mais competição, tensão e decisões estratégicas. E um jogo divertido que te deixará a pensar no que ira vir nos próximos anos.

reviews.review:
[b]brave hand[/b] is an endless score-attack card game with a bit of a narrative that has been on mobile devices for years, then finally made its way to pc in 2021. unfortunately, [b]the quality of the port is poor[/b].

there's a how to play section and a tutorial, but here's the gist: the game is a [b]solitaire-like with some other stuff[/b]. you're provided with 7 cards and have to place them over 8 piles, each with an increasing number of cards, hoping that yours is bigger than the one on top of the pile of your choice (tie means you lose). if it is, you can either collect the points, get a new card from the deck and go for another pile (or the same with a different card), or push your luck with the same pile and card (risk/reward situation, losing means no new card). clearing a stack gives some sort of bonus (cash, multiplier, extra cards, etc.) and if you get rid of all the cards, you win, but even losing awards coins for 'captured' cards.

the deck consists of 52 regular cards, suit doesn't matter (doesn't exist, in fact), and the 'some other stuff' includes 2 demon cards on top of the other 52. they're worth 15, an ace is 14, and 2 beats ace but obviously not much else. cards can also be sacrificed to roll a dice and reveal the top of two piles, along with their stack bonus.

[b]5 game modes[/b] are available. I've just described the default [u]brave[/u], then there's [u]jumbo deck[/u] with 90 cards in the deck and 8 in each pile, [u]boost[/u] lets you add special cards to the deck in exchange for some money, and [u]zen[/u] is more lenient (tie means win, new card even if you lose). [u]dungeon run[/u] got added after release, with a bigger deck serving as health. an empty hand doesn't mean game over here, you can keep clearing floors until the deck runs out, with every 3rd being a campsite that restores some health if completed. then you get a combined score after game over.

[b]online leaderboards[/b] are available for every mode and money can be used in the [b]collection[/b] menu (referred to as the 'treasure room' in the how to play section for some reason) to [b]unlock alternate themes and story bits[/b] with way too many clicks. story pages unlock the rest of the game modes too.

[b]the presentation is really nice[/b], pretty backgrounds with matching colors for the game board, good if repetitive music, but it's in portrait mode and [b]widescreen is lazily handled by placing zoomed-in pieces of the current background on both sides[/b]. far from ideal, but hey, no black bars...

[b]settings are a mixed bag too.[/b] the game's offered in many languages, there's a background animation toggle and one for messy piles (otherwise they're organized neatly), plus windowed mode and resolution options. however, there's [b]only a single audio toggle[/b], no way to turn music or sound off separately, nor to decrease their deafening volume.

these options are only available from the main menu and clicking the achievements and leaderboards buttons only brings up the steam overlay, which matches the other laziness nicely. and of course tap tap tap fucking everywhere and [b]free coins every 15 minutes, folks![/b] it eventually goes up to 30 minutes, then an hour, as if we're still on mobile.

while it gets repetitive fast, it's [b]good fun for a while and only $2, but it's free on mobile[/b]. and for a port, not even a game from scratch, supposedly in development (or development hell) for years, [b]missing functionality and all the mobile shenanigans are problematic[/b]. it shouldn't be hard to make some quick adjustments for a better experience, but it remains to be seen if the developer's willing and able or not.
